question: Why did the p95 latency go up on 12 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: The flash sale campaign went live, causing a surge in traffic and errors.
why_chain: The flash sale campaign increased the number of requests and errors.
The increased traffic overwhelmed the system, leading to higher latency and error rates.
The system could not handle the sudden increase in load, resulting in the observed latency and error rates.

contributing_factors.description: The system was already under stress due to the flash sale campaign.
why_chain: The system was already under stress due to the flash sale campaign.
The system could not scale quickly enough to handle the increased load.
The deployment of catalog v6.12 and checkout v1.8 did not address the root cause of the issue.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The deployment of catalog v6.12 and checkout v1.8 caused the issue.
ruled_out.reason: The deployments were in different regions and were routine releases, not related to the observed issue.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The autoscaler scaling out caused the issue.
ruled_out.reason: The autoscaler scaling out occurred after the change, and the issue was already present.

evidence.summary: P95 latency for region ap-south rose from 137 ms to 252 ms (+84%), with a change point at 2026-03-12T06:35:00Z.
The change is concentrated in region ap-south: 4 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.01).
At the same time, request volume for region ap-south rose (1235 per 5 min before, 4430 per 5 min after, +259%).
At the same time, error rate for region ap-south rose (0.38% before, 0.76% after, +101%).
Marketing: flash sale campaign goes live in ap-south at 06:35 UTC (ap-south; 288 min before the change; record R010; fit: right time and place: a strong candidate cause)
Request volume 3x normal in ap-south (ap-south; 12 min after the change; record R014; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)
autoscaler: scaling out, 4 new instances requested (ap-south; 20 min after the change; record R015; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)
Deployed catalog v6.12 to us-east (catalog, us-east; 3 min before the change; record R013; fit: different service/region, so unlikely to be the cause)
Deployed checkout v1.8 to us-east (routine release) (checkout, us-east; 272 min before the change; record R011; fit: different service/region, so unlikely to be the cause)

reasons: ✓ A change event (tickets) lines up in time (288 min before the change).
✓ 2 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✓ Request volume rose, as a traffic cause requires.
✓ No competing change event fits as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.

actions.action: Implement traffic management and load balancing to handle sudden spikes in traffic.
Optimize the system's capacity and performance to handle the expected traffic during campaigns.
Monitor and analyze the system's performance during campaigns to identify and address potential issues proactively.
